question: Which atomic number is related with four valence electrons?
solution:
The correct answer is __**6.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** atomic number **of an element **tells us the number of protons in the nucleus** of an atom of that element.
 
• The atomic number related with four valence electrons is 6. 
 
• Carbon have atomic number 6 and four valence electrons.
 
• **In an electrically neutral atom**, the number of protons is equal to the number of electrons.
 
 
• Therefore, the atomic number also tells us the number of electrons in a neutral atom of that element.
 
 
 
• **Valence electrons are the outermost electrons in an atom** that participate in chemical bonding.
 
• The number of valence electrons **determines the chemical properties of an element.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**Carbon:

 
• It is a chemical element that is nonmetallic and belongs to Periodic Table Group 14 (IVa).
 
• In terms of weight, carbon is ranked 19th among the elements that are abundant in the crust of Earth.
 
• It forms compounds by covalent bond.
 
• Graphite differs because all of its carbon atoms are sp² hybridized, which results in delocalized free electrons.
 
• It is tetravalent and can form four covalent bonds.
